title: Capital Letters and Full Stops (KS1)
subject: English
strapline: Where a sentence starts, where it ends, and the four end marks.
facts: Every sentence begins with a capital letter.
A statement (telling sentence) ends with a full stop: "We went to the park."
A question ends with a question mark: "Where is my hat?"
A sentence showing strong feeling can end with an exclamation mark: "What a mess!"
Always use a capital letter for the word "I", for names, days, months and places.
A full stop tells the reader to take a small pause and shows one idea has finished.
When you check your writing, read it aloud — your voice drops where a full stop should go.

quick_quiz.q: What mark ends the sentence "Do you like cake"?
Which letter always needs a capital when it means yourself?
What must every sentence start with?

teacher_tips: Use "capital letter hunts" in a shared book before expecting them in writing.
A finger-space, capital, full stop checklist at the desk builds independence.
Model editing your own writing with a coloured pen so mistakes feel normal.
